title: mchen-embed-dim-spike-sleuth-scratchpad
body:
Quick scratchpad — chasing two linked problems seen in prod rerank path: 1) intermittent embedding dimension mismatch errors, and 2) tail latency spikes (p95/p99) on rerank step. Notes + commands I ran + raw error snippets + hypotheses.

SUMMARY
- First saw alerts Mar 9: multiple jobs failing rerank with "Expected embedding dim 1536 but got 1024". Around same time (within minutes) we had p95 jump from ~120ms to ~600ms for rerank endpoint for a handful of customers. Not consistent across Customers A/B.
- Impact: transient failures for ranking pipelines (fallback to coarse sort), increased user-facing latency and some retries.

TIMELINE (observed)
- 2026-03-08 22:41 UTC: Canary run for embed-upgrade finished, no obvious errors.
- 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC: Customer A alert: 18% of requests returned 500 with dim mismatch.
- 2026-03-09 03:15 UTC: We also saw rerank p99 jump to 2.1s for ~10m.
- 2026-03-09 03:50 UTC: Temporary mitigation: increased client-side timeout + disabled new embed model in customer config. Errors reduced.

OBSERVATIONS / METRICS
- Error rate correlates with traffic to model variant "embed-open-1536-quant" (sampled logs).
- Most errors show 1024 vecs returned; a small fraction show 0-length vectors.
- FAISS index ingestion logs show occasional truncation warnings during bulk-upsert windows (daily batch at 03:00 UTC).
- Rerank p95 correlates with CPU spikes on the rerank-service pods (GOMAXPROCS saturation) and longer database latency for the ranking candidates table.

COMMANDS / QUICK REPRO / TRACES I RAN
- Curl to embeddings endpoint (manual sanity):
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"embed-open-1536-quant","input":"test sentence for dims"}' | jq .
  -> returned array length 1536 for most calls, but on ~1/20 calls length 1024 (see raw-out-0309.txt)

- Python using SDK (local repro):
  from redwood import Client
  c = Client(token=os.getenv('TOKEN'))
  r = c.embeddings.create(model='embed-open-1536-quant', input='hi')
  print(len(r.data[0].embedding))
  -> 1024 in failing case

- Check index with faiss inspect (local copy of index from snapshot):
  python tools/inspect_index_dims.py --index-path gs://prod-embeddings/customer-a/2026-03-09-03 --expect-dim 1536
  -> prints many entries "dim=1024" and some warnings about "vector truncated during serialization"

- Rerank endpoint repro to capture timing + traces:
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank?model=rerank-v1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @small-candidate-payload.json -w '\\nTIME:%{time_total}'
  -> TIME:0.65 (failing run) / TIME:0.11 (normal run). Collected x-ray trace ids -> trace: trace-20260309-0315-01

RAW ERROR SNIPPETS (collected)
- ValueError: Expected embedding dim 1536, got 1024
- WARNING faiss.index: Found vector length mismatch during add, skipping vector id=45321
- rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded
- rerank-service[pid=4231]: batch 34 processing took 1.8s (normal ~0.08s)

HYPOTHESES (ranked)
1) Upstream model variant "embed-open-1536-quant" accidentally served a 1024-dim variant (model artifact mixup) during rolling rollout.
   - Evidence: errors coincide with rollout window and requests hitting specific shard hosts.
   - Test: pin to older model id / check model binary hashes on hosts 10.4.2.*.
2) Embedding post-processing step (quantization/post-merge) truncates vectors when quantizing in certain GPUs to reduce memory, bug in serialization code.
   - Evidence: "vector truncated during serialization" in index inspector logs.
   - Test: re-run serialization locally with tool and compare binary length.
3) Client SDK or pipelined consumer upgraded and changed default model param (e.g., switched from 1536->1024 for speed) causing consumers to send different dims into rerank cluster that expects 1536.
   - Evidence: a small subset of customers use new SDK version.
   - Test: correlate user agent and SDK version in logs with error occurrences.
4) FAISS ingestion job had a transient bug during the daily bulk-upsert that wrote 1024-dim vectors into a 1536-dim index (index acceptor tolerated shorter vectors but later crashed on read).
   - Evidence: ingestion warnings, timing alignment with daily batch.
   - Test: check upsert job logs and confirm vector sizes at write time.
5) Resource pressure causing partial responses (stream cutoff) leading to truncated embeddings (rare, but plausible under extreme memory pressure).
   - Evidence: paired with rerank CPU/RAM spikes.
   - Test: reproduce under artificially constrained env (cgroup memlimit).

WHAT I TRIED (mitigations)
- Rolled back model variant for affected customers -> errors dropped.
- Increased rerank timeouts temporarily and added defensive check to drop mismatched-dim vectors before scoring.
- Re-ran FAISS ingestion for one affected shard from backup -> index now shows correct 1536 dims.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs
- Which hosts served the 1024 variant? (need model artifact hash compare across nodes)
- Is there a subtle serialization path when quantizing to int8 that loses 512 dims? (weird but logs show truncation)
- Why do some users still see p95 spikes after rollback? (maybe rerank-service cache / sticky routing)
- Are there SDKs that silently changed default model param? version map is incomplete.

IMMEDIATE NEXT STEPS (priority order)
- (P0) Collate host-level model artifact hashes for all embed-serving hosts for March 9 02:00-04:00 UTC. (assign: @daniel)
- (P0) Re-run ingestion-check on all shards touched by daily upsert and mark any truncated indexes for reingest. (assign: @ethan)
- (P1) Add defensive sanity check at rerank ingress to log/metric and drop vectors with unexpected dims (short-term only).
- (P1) Add SDK telemetry query to find clients that switched model param in last 7d.
- (P2) Add unit test to embedding serialization code to ensure binary length != expected_dim triggers hard fail.

NOTES TO SELF
- Keep copies of raw failing embeddings (raw-out-0309.txt) in /tmp/mchen-embeds/ for offline bisect. Don't `rm` them.
- When asking infra for pcap/trace, include time window +/- 10m.
- If rolling back again, prefer circular canary (10% traffic) not full rollback to reduce blast radius.

REFERENCES (internal)
- Slack thread: #infra-embeddings "mar9 dim-truncation" (link above)
- GH PR with suspected serialization change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/services/pull/3125
- Linear ticket that tracks reingest: https://linear.app/ENG/issue/ENG-2187

-- end scratchpad --

(Will update after host artifact list from @Daniel and reingest status from @Ethan.)
